text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- A dispute between the four-week National Reconciliation government and President Sali Berisha over the sacking of a deputy interior minister might be the start of a deeper crisis.
- Fleeing former defence minister Safet Zhulali says he had told Berisha to find political ways to solve the crisis in the country rather than apply a state of emergency.
- The National Intellegence Service (SHIK) has not yet a new chief because Berisha has refused to accept candidates for the job proposed by the opposition Socialists.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- An explosive device blew up a parked car belonging to Tirana deputy police chief Arben Ujka in central Tirana on Tuesday.
- A group of dissidents from the Democratic Party will form a new party, called the Movement for Democracy.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino has accepted his cabinet did not know the deputy interior minister they sacked had been named by decree but will ask the president to approve his dismissal.
- Parliament, dominated by the Democratic Party, approved a law which empowers the interior minister to propose prefects and gives them bigger powers over local government.
- Franco Passacatando, an executive director of the World Bank, has said Albania should immediately shut down the alleged pyramid schemes before donors will help.
ALBANIA
- The paper accuses Finance Minister Arben Malaj of founding two alleged pyramid schemes. Malaj has said he would audit surviving firms that pay high interest.

- The supervising council of the Bank of Albania has recommended to President Berisha the sacking of governor Kristaq Luniku, who is currently in Washington working on a IMF-assistance programme for Albania.
- Maksude Kadema, the 32-year-old gypsy who was arrested after declaring her pyramid scheme was bankrupt, has said she might have a chance to pay back her 10,000 creditors if freed from jail.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The paper accuses the Socialist Party of intensifying a propaganda against Democratic Party administration officials.
- Austria will send 115 policemen and soldiers to Albania. The Austrians will guard the local seat of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
- Deputy interior minister Agim Shehu has filed a suit with the Constitutional Court to reverse a government decision ordering his dismissal.
ZERI I POPULLIT

- The paper questions who is trying to endanger the relations of policemen with the National Reconciliation government. It says the Finance Ministry has allocated funds to pay policemen promised wages but they have not yet received any money.
- Three opposition party leaders support the government decision to sack the deputy interior minister.
